A Q&A session video from one of Apple's most talked-about events in the past 20 years has surfaced online — catch it before it gets taken down. See below.

Watch it before Apple pulls the video

Even if you weren't paying close attention to Apple back in 2010, you've probably heard of the "Antennagate" scandal — and how Steve Jobs, who was on holiday in Hawaii, was hastily called back to hold a press conference.

If you only learned about this later, here's what happened: shortly after the iPhone 4 went on sale, users found that the way they held the phone caused the cellular signal to drop dramatically.

The controversy blew up to the point that Apple had to hastily organise an event just a few weeks after the iPhone 4 launched.

At the event, Jobs explained that signal attenuation wasn't a problem unique to the iPhone 4, and that users could either get a free case to prevent their palm from touching the antenna directly, or return the phone for a full refund.

After the event, Jobs, along with then-COO Tim Cook and Apple's Senior Vice President of Mac Hardware Engineering Bob Mansfield, took questions from the media together.

Since then, there have been plenty of accounts of what was said that day — including John Gruber's recollection of asking a question that made Jobs, Cook and Mansfield pull a caseless iPhone 4 out of their pockets, producing one of the most memorable photos of that era. But the original footage of the Q&A session has never surfaced. Until now.

Earlier this week, the YouTube channel Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (which appears to have nothing to do with the real Sir Mix-A-Lot) uploaded the entire 47-minute Q&A session video, which you can watch below:

It's not yet known how the video was obtained, nor whether Apple will file a copyright takedown request. But now that it's out there, even if the original upload is deleted, copies will easily resurface elsewhere.

The fact that the video is still viewable right now is already a good sign. Still, if you want to see this piece of Apple history with your own eyes, you'd better hurry.

Were you following Apple back during the "Antennagate" days? Feel free to share your memories in the comments.
